topic.title: Marvel Pledged Its Heroes' Film Rights for a Movie Loan

title: Marvel Put Captain America Up as Collateral
description:
Why would Marvel hand a bank the film rights to Captain America?
Marvel went bankrupt in 1996, then borrowed $525M to make its own films, with the rights to 10 characters as the security. Then came Iron Man, and Disney.
Sources: Marvel Entertainment 10-K, The Walt Disney Company (Aug 2009).
Based on public records and reporting. Not financial or legal advice.

cta: Iron Man or Captain America: which hero saved Marvel? Comment

lines.text: Marvel borrowed to make its own movies, and the security was Captain America.
The decade before, Marvel had gone bankrupt.
Its biggest heroes were out on licence: Spider-Man at Sony, the X-Men at Fox. So how could it make its own films?
So Marvel took a $525M credit line, arranged by Merrill Lynch.
Its filing says the film rights to 10 characters were pledged as collateral, Captain America and the Avengers among them.
Black Panther and Doctor Strange were on the list too. So what would Marvel film first?
Its first film was Iron Man, starring Robert Downey Junior, and that same loan paid for it.
Then Disney came, offering $30 a share in cash, plus stock, for more than 5,000 characters.
In all, Disney agreed to pay about $4B for the company that had pledged its own heroes.
Iron Man or Captain America: which hero saved Marvel? Next time you see the Avengers, remember,

Beat 'ironman' (and the ending's 'Iron Man or the bank loan'): says Iron Man was 'a hero who was not on that list', framing Iron Man as separate from the loan. Marvel's FY2008 10-K (sec.gov .../000136231009002976/c81637e10vk.htm) lists Iron Man and The Incredible Hulk among the characters whose theatrical film rights are pledged as collateral, and says 'Borrowings have been used to fund direct production costs of our Iron Man and The Incredible Hulk feature films' from the $525 million facility. True of the 2005 list only; as told it misleads (rule 3). Fix: say Iron Man was added to the pledge later / was paid for with that same loan, and recast the ending's either/or (e.g. the loan paid for Iron Man).

All six sourced facts confirmed: $525M, $465M senior (+$60M mezzanine) and ten pledged characters incl. Captain America, Avengers, Black Panther, Doctor Strange on the FY2005 10-K page; ~$4B, $30/share cash plus stock, more than 5,000 characters, 31 Aug 2009 on the Disney press release. Merrill Lynch as arranger is not in the 10-K but is in Marvel's own 8-K (Sept 2005, 'arranged by Merrill Lynch Commercial Finance Corp.'). Bankruptcy 1996 (MEG) and Iron Man 2 May 2008 OK; disclaimer present.
